consent.label: BEFORE WE BEGIN
consent.p1: Nola gives health information, not a diagnosis. It's not for emergencies. Call 112 if you need urgent help.
consent.p2: To understand you, your voice is processed by Sarvam AI and your messages by an AI model hosted on Groq. Your voice recordings are never stored. Your chats are saved encrypted on our servers so you can come back to them and make doctor-visit reports; you can delete one chat or everything, any time.
consent.p3: Designed around consent, purpose limitation, and data minimisation, in the spirit of India's DPDP Act, 2023.

learn.rename: On 12 May 2026, PCOS was renamed Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS) through a global consensus published in The Lancet. The new name moves the focus away from "cysts" and toward hormones and metabolism. The change happens over 3 years.

cal.title: Your cycle
cal.phaseTap: Tap a phase to see its days on the calendar.

pd.menstrual: Your period. The womb lining sheds. Rest, warmth and gentle movement help.
pd.follicular: Oestrogen rises after your period. Energy and mood often lift.
pd.ovulation: An egg is released around now. Your most fertile days (an estimate).
pd.luteal: Progesterone rises. Bloating, cravings or mood changes are common before your period.

cal.lateHint: Tap “My period started” when it comes. If it is often late, it is worth talking to a doctor.

moves.lede: Gentle stretches that may ease cramps, back ache and stress. Tap one to practise with Nola's timer.
moves.ready: Press start when you're in position
moves.safety: Move slowly and never into pain. Stop if anything hurts, and check with a doctor if you are pregnant or recovering from an injury.

child.name: Child's pose
child.why: Softens the lower back and belly, a calm place to rest during cramps.
child.steps: Kneel, big toes together, knees a little apart.|Sit back towards your heels.|Walk your hands forward and rest your forehead down.|Let your belly soften with each slow breath.

catcow.name: Cat–cow
catcow.why: Warms up the spine and may ease period back ache and stiffness.
catcow.steps: Come onto hands and knees, wrists under shoulders, knees under hips.|Breathe in: let the belly drop and lift your gaze (cow).|Breathe out: round your back up and tuck your chin (cat).|Move slowly with each breath.

happybaby.name: Happy baby
happybaby.why: Gently opens the hips and releases the lower back.
happybaby.steps: Lie on your back and hug your knees in.|Hold the outsides of your feet, soles facing the ceiling.|Draw your knees towards your armpits.|Rock softly from side to side.

bridge.name: Bridge pose
bridge.why: Strengthens the hips and lower back and opens the front of the body.
bridge.steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart.|Breathe in: press through your feet and lift your hips.|Breathe out: lower slowly, one part of the spine at a time.|Keep your neck relaxed and still.

food.lede: Small food habits that may help your energy, cramps and mood through the month.
food.waterSub: Tap a glass each time you drink one.
food.note: General healthy-eating tips, not a diet plan. If you have diabetes, thyroid or another condition, ask your doctor what suits you.

phaseNote.menstrual: During your period, focus on iron, warmth and rest.
phaseNote.follicular: Energy is rising: fresh, fibre-rich meals keep it steady.
phaseNote.ovulation: Plenty of water, fibre and healthy fats help around ovulation.
phaseNote.luteal: Before your period, steady meals and less salt and sugar may ease cravings and bloating.

water.title: Drink more water
water.line: Aim for about 8 glasses a day.
water.why: Staying hydrated can ease bloating, headaches and tiredness.
water.try: Keep a bottle nearby. Coconut water, jeera water, buttermilk and soups count too.

caffeine.title: Cut down on caffeine
caffeine.line: Fewer cups of tea, coffee and cola.
caffeine.why: A lot of caffeine may make cramps, breast tenderness, anxiety and poor sleep worse.
caffeine.try: Swap one cup for ginger, tulsi or chamomile tea, and skip caffeine after 3 pm.

iron.title: Eat iron-rich foods
iron.line: Replace the iron your period takes.
iron.why: You lose iron with every period, and low iron can leave you tired and breathless.
iron.try: Palak, rajma, chana, dates, jaggery, ragi and eggs. Add lemon or amla to help your body absorb it.

grains.title: Choose whole grains and fibre
grains.line: Millets, dal and vegetables every day.
grains.why: Fibre keeps blood sugar steady, which matters especially with PMOS.
grains.try: Ragi, jowar or bajra rotis, brown rice, oats, dal and a vegetable with every meal.

sugar.title: Go easy on sugar and maida
sugar.line: Fewer sweets, biscuits and white bread.
sugar.why: Sugary snacks spike and crash your energy and may worsen mood swings and cravings.
sugar.try: Reach for fruit, roasted chana, makhana or a handful of nuts instead.

magnesium.title: Magnesium for cramps
magnesium.why: Magnesium-rich foods may help ease cramps and PMS symptoms.
magnesium.try: Pumpkin seeds, bananas, peanuts, spinach, and a small piece of dark chocolate.

fats.title: Add healthy fats
fats.why: Omega-3 fats may help with period pain and inflammation.
fats.try: Flaxseed (alsi), walnuts, chia seeds, and fish if you eat it.

salt.title: Less salt before your period
salt.why: Salt makes your body hold water, which can add to bloating.
salt.try: In the week before your period, cut back on pickles, papad, chips and packaged snacks.

protein.title: Protein at every meal
protein.why: Protein helps keep blood sugar and energy even through the day.
protein.try: Dal, paneer, curd, eggs, sprouts, tofu or chicken.
